denver-colorado-rockies-golden-gate-cany.speedBand: 50–80 km/h riding core, local limits always win

sections.advice: This High point near Evergreen → Near Applewood stretch is for rhythm and scenery. Keep your head up, let the view breathe, and resist turning every open bend into a target. Stop once properly rather than half-stopping everywhere.

Scenic stretch near Erie → Photo stop near Firestone is the technical section. Hairpins, gradients and mixed traffic can stack up quickly; use low drama inputs, stay wide of centre lines and expect buses or riders appearing exactly where optimism says they will not.

Photo stop near Firestone → Denver / Colorado Rockies return can flow quickly, but only if you keep village limits and junction sightlines sacred. Fast connectors are where rides get untidy when fatigue creeps in.

sections.photoQuery: Denver / Colorado Rockies return Golden Gate Canyon Dawn checkpoint 8 Denver / Colorado Rockies
sections.advice: Use Denver / Colorado Rockies return → Food stop near Ponderosa Park as clean positioning. Keep it tidy, ignore impatient traffic and save the enthusiasm for the good road ahead. The value here is not drama; it is arriving at the riding section with space, fuel and concentration intact.

Food stop near Ponderosa Park → Back to Golden Gate is the logistics leg. Watch junctions, villages and speed changes, then let the roadbook do its job: move you out of the clutter without spending your best attention too early.
